{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (HDI Hosting/Development Agreement)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review — verified findings, redlines and walk-away exposure

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and identified **18 findings: 3 critical, 6 high, 8 medium and 1 low**. Seven positions are compliant and require no redline; six are deviations requiring the proposed edits; five clauses the playbook expects are missing entirely.

The principal problem is not bad drafting but absent drafting. The Agreement has **no indemnification provision, no ownership/IP provision, no limitation of liability, no performance warranty, no post-termination transition or data-return obligation, and no insurance covenant** — despite HDI designing, hosting and maintaining the Site and holding our Content, user information and customer/order data. Both parties are exposed to unlimited direct and consequential damages, we have no stated ownership of the Site deliverables or our own customer data, and there is no contractual route to get that data back on exit.

On the commercial terms, the Agreement is asymmetric against us in three linked respects: the **Section 6.1 exclusivity** covenant binds us for an open-ended, auto-renewing term with no performance-based release; the **Section 4.2(a) Termination Payment** (12 months' Net Sales less $800,000, halved) is uncapped, far exceeds three months' fees and applies even where we terminate for HDI's breach; and the **Section 4.1** non-renewal window is 90 days, above the fallback ceiling. HDI's **Section 3.4** records inspection right carries no frequency cap.

On the positive side, the fee structure is purely usage-based with no minimum commitment, there is no MFN and no non-solicit binding us, governing law is New York (our preferred position), and HDI's own two-year non-compete tail in Section 6.3 runs in our favour. We have left all of these untouched.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue and our position |
|---|----------|------|--------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | New §9A (after §9 Warranties) | No indemnity, hold-harmless or defense language anywhere; the document moves from the mutual warranties in §9 to General Provisions in §10. HDI owes nothing for third-party IP claims, breach of law, breach of the §8 confidentiality/customer-data obligations, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct. **Walk-away territory** (no vendor IP indemnity at all). Insert §9A with HDI indemnity, a narrow reciprocal Company indemnity limited to Content and Marks we supply and our own breach of law, plus standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | New §5.5 | No ownership or IP clause. HDI develops and hosts the Site (§§1.1–1.3) and holds our Content, user information and order data (§8.1), yet nothing says who owns the deliverables, Content or customer data. §5.2 gives us artistic and editorial control but not ownership; the §6.1 trademark licence is properly narrow and benefits us. Fallback not met (no licence-back either). Insert §5.5: Company owns Site deliverables, Content, Marks and Company Data; HDI retains pre-existing platform IP subject to a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to us; no joint ownership. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | End of §9 (to pick up existing survival) | No liability cap, damages exclusion or aggregate-liability language anywhere; §9 Warranties and §10 General Provisions are silent. Both parties face unlimited direct and consequential damages. Insert the preferred mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees (the 30% of Net Sales payable under §3, a meaningful base) and USD 1,000,000, with uncapped carve-outs for confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirmation that our payment obligations sit outside the cap. |
| 4 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | §6.1 (with §§4.1, 4.2(a), 1.6, 6.2, 6.3) | §6.1 bars us from any similar Internet project for Deerskin Products or "products substantially similar", and gives HDI the exclusive online right to the Deerskin brand. Fails the fallback on two material terms: (i) it runs for the term, which auto-renews annually under §4.1, so the lock-up is open-ended, and our only exit triggers the §4.2(a) Termination Payment; and (ii) there is no performance-based release — no service levels, no termination for breach, and §1.6 is a one-off launch-date exit only. Scope also reaches competitor-type goods. §6.2 closeout carve-out and HDI's reciprocal §6.3 covenant mitigate but do not cure. Propose the fallback rather than deletion: narrow to Deerskin Products, cap at 12 months from the Effective Date, automatic release with no Termination Payment on HDI's failure to meet its Article 1 obligations. |
| 5 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | §4.2(a) (cf. §3.1, §4.2(c)) | The Termination Payment applies whenever we terminate and is 50% of the preceding 12 months' Net Sales above $800,000, against fees of only 30% of Net Sales above $11,000/month. On a one-year term terminable on 90 days' notice it can substantially exceed both three months' fees and remaining contract value, and it bites even where we terminate for HDI's breach. Fails the fallback (3 months' fees) and **approaches walk-away territory**. Propose the fallback: cap at three months' §3.1 fees, sole amount payable, disapplied where we terminate for HDI's breach. §4.2(c) instalment mechanic unaffected. |
| 6 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | §4.1 / §4.2(a) | The 90-day convenience right in §4.1 sits at the low end of the fallback for both parties and is not flagged. The material failure is §4.2(a): our exit is not "without penalty" and the Termination Payment (12 months' Net Sales less $800,000, halved, over eight quarterly instalments) is uncapped and dwarfs the three-month fee ceiling. Adopt the fallback fee cap rather than deleting the payment, given the revenue-share bargain and the negotiated $800,000 threshold. |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | §1.4 (cf. §6.1, §10.3) | §1.4 is the only grant running to us (access to and use of HDI's hosting system, software and Content administration tools). It names only "the Company" — our affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf are neither included nor addable by notice, which fails the fallback on a material term. The licence is not revocable at HDI's discretion, and §10.3 carries the Agreement to successors, satisfying transferability. Add affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf and confirm the rights are irrevocable during the term. |
| 8 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | §10.3 (cf. §4 termination rights) | §10.3 is a bare successors-and-assigns provision with no consent standard in either direction. No walk-away triggers (our assignment freedom is not blocked; no HDI change-of-control termination or re-pricing right). It fails the fallback because consent (not unreasonably withheld) is still required for non-successor assignments: as drafted HDI may freely transfer this hosting arrangement — including access to Company data and the licensed Deerskin Marks — to any third party, including a competitor. Add an affiliate/M&A-successor carve-out for us, a reasonable-consent gate plus no-competitor limit on HDI assignments, and confirm a Company change of control gives HDI no rights. |
| 9 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant (fallback) | §6 (§§6.1–6.3, cf. §§1.1, 4.1) | Binds us but sits at the fallback: term-only with no post-term tail (the two-year tail in §6.3 runs against HDI, to our benefit), terminable on 90 days' notice under §4.1, confined to a named product line and named competitors rather than "any competing business", and carved back by §6.2 (closeout merchandise) and the §1.1 definition of Deerskin Products (excludes closeout merchandise and the Joan Cook Catalog). Noted for the record but not redlined: the elastic reach of "products substantially similar"/"companies similar to", and the absence of an express carve-out for internal development and acquisitions. |
| 10 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | §9 (new §9(c)); cf. §1.6 | §9 contains only mutual corporate-existence/authority representations and a Globix Agreement acknowledgement. HDI gives no warranty on the quality or conformance of its development or hosting work: no workmanlike standard, no conformance period, no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty, and no repair/re-perform/refund remedy. §1.6 is a go-live termination right, not a warranty. Fails even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies); mitigated only by the absence of any disclaimer, so not full "AS IS" walk-away territory. Insert §9(c) with the preferred warranty set and a real remedy (re-performance, repair/replacement or refund, plus termination without Termination Payment on failure to cure); a 90-day conformance period is an acceptable landing zone. |
| 11 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | New §4.3 (cf. §§1.5, 8.1–8.3, 10.7) | §4 addresses only notice periods and the Termination Payment; no exit obligations. §1.5 export files apply only during operation, §§8.1–8.3 impose no return or destruction duty, and the §10.7 survival clause omits §§4, 5 and 8. HDI hosts the Site and holds our Content, user information and customer/order data, so the Agreement falls below even the fallback and **risks the walk-away outcome of no data return**. Insert §4.3 at the preferred position: up to six months' transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of Content and customer/order data in machine-readable format within 30 days of the Termination Date, certified deletion thereafter. |
| 12 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | §4.1 | One-year automatic renewals (acceptable length) but a 90-day non-renewal notice requirement, above the 60-day fallback ceiling; short of walk-away territory. Move to the preferred 30-day window, with 60 days as the fallback. No renewal price-uplift language, so no cap needed; absence of a vendor renewal reminder is noted only. |
| 13 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | §3.4 (cf. §8.2) | §3.4 meets or beats the playbook on most terms: 30 days' prior written notice, limited to payment-calculation records during our normal business hours, HDI bears all inspection costs unconditionally. But it has **no frequency limit at all**, failing both the preferred and fallback positions and approaching the walk-away position on unlimited audits. Insert a once-per-twelve-month cap and change nothing else. Noted not flagged: inspection by HDI's General Manager rather than an independent auditor, and no restated confidentiality (covered by §8.2). |
| 14 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | §10.5 | New York law, conflict-of-laws principles expressly disapplied — our preferred governing law. No arbitration provision anywhere and no foreign exclusive venue, so disputes default to the courts. Only shortfall is the absence of an express exclusive-venue designation for the state and federal courts in New York County; a missing mechanic, not a material failure. We would add the venue sentence if the document is opened for other reasons, but it does not warrant a standalone redline. |
| 15 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | §3 (cf. §§6.1, 6.2) | No MFN or best-terms mechanic in either direction. §3 economics are a fixed revenue share of Net Sales with no obligation to match third-party terms, extend better pricing or match competing offers. The §6.1 exclusivity is a scope restriction addressed under the exclusivity rule, not an MFN. Meets the preferred position; no redline. Noted only: there is also no MFN in our favour. |
| 16 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | §§3.1, 3.3, 4.1 | Preferred position met: we owe only a 30% share of actual Net Sales above an $11,000 monthly threshold — purely usage-based. No minimum spend, guaranteed volume, take-or-pay or shortfall/true-up penalty; §3.3 provides only a refunds-and-exchanges reconciliation in our favour, and §4.1 gives a clean annual exit on 90 days' notice. The §4.2 Termination Payment is an exit fee (see items 5 and 6) and §6.1 restricts channels rather than volumes (item 4). |
| 17 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | §10.2 | No restrictive covenant on hiring or soliciting either party's employees anywhere in the Agreement. The only employment-related language is the independent-contractor/no-joint-venture provision in §10.2, which does not restrict us from soliciting or hiring HDI personnel. Meets the preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer); no redline. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | New §10.9 (cf. §10.7) | No insurance covenant anywhere; §10 covers notices, no joint venture, assignment, waiver, governing law, severability, survival, entire agreement and headings only. HDI hosts the Site on its own server and expressly may have access to Content, user information, data and our Confidential Information. Under the rule this is **walk-away territory** (no insurance for a vendor that processes personal data). Insert §10.9: CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M while HDI hosts the Site or holds Confidential Information or user data, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request. §10.7 survival already carries §10 for two years, consistent with the one-year tail. Fallback landing zone: E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following findings sit in, approach, or risk the playbook's walk-away territory and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than negotiable preferences:

1. **No vendor indemnity at all (item 1, INDEMN — critical).** The complete absence of any IP indemnity is expressly walk-away under the rule. HDI must accept the §9A package.
2. **No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data (item 18, INSURANCE).** Walk-away under the rule; HDI hosts the Site and holds user information. The E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback is available as a landing zone, but some cyber cover is non-negotiable.
3. **No data return on exit (item 11, TRANSITION).** The Agreement falls below the fallback and risks the walk-away outcome of no data return, with §10.7 survival omitting §§4, 5 and 8. We must have the §4.3 return-and-deletion obligation.
4. **Uncapped Termination Payment (items 5 and 6, LD / T4C).** The §4.2(a) payment approaches walk-away territory: it is uncapped, can exceed remaining contract value, and applies even when we terminate for HDI's breach. At minimum it must be disapplied on HDI breach.
5. **Unlimited inspection frequency (item 13, AUDIT).** §3.4 has no frequency cap at all, approaching the walk-away position on unlimited audits. A once-per-twelve-month cap is a minimal, low-cost fix.
6. **Unlimited liability with no cap and nothing to carve out (item 3, LOL-CAP).** Exposure to unlimited direct and consequential damages is not acceptable, and the cap and the indemnity in item 1 should be negotiated together.
7. **No ownership of our own customer data or the Site deliverables (item 2, IP).** Read with item 11, we currently have neither title to nor a contractual right to recover the data HDI holds.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the six deviations (items 4–8, 10, 12, 13) and the five insertions (new §§4.3, 5.5, 9A, 9(c), 10.9 and the liability cap at the end of §9). Comments to carry the `[Playbook]` prefix, state the playbook position in one or two sentences, and offer the identified fallbacks.
2. **Sequence the negotiation around the linked risk-allocation package** — indemnity (item 1), liability cap (item 3), warranty (item 10) and insurance (item 18) — and present it as a single package rather than four separate asks, since the cap carve-outs depend on the indemnity existing.
3. **Treat exclusivity and the exit economics as one commercial trade** (items 4, 5, 6). Our ask is the fallback in each case: exclusivity narrowed to Deerskin Products and capped at 12 months with an automatic performance-based release, and the Termination Payment capped at three months' §3.1 fees and disapplied on HDI breach. Confirm with the business the value of HDI's reciprocal §6.3 covenant before conceding on the cap.
4. **Confirm the data position with the business and IT**: what Content, user information and customer/order data HDI will hold, and in what format we would need it returned, so the §4.3 export specification and the cyber cover limit in §10.9 are calibrated to actual exposure.
5. **Hold the low-cost items for the same turn**: the §3.4 once-per-year inspection cap, the §4.1 30-day non-renewal window, the §1.4 extension to affiliates and contractors, and the §10.3 assignment consent gate and no-competitor limit. We would also add the New York County exclusive-venue sentence to §10.5 while the document is open, though it does not justify a standalone redline.
6. **No action** on the compliant positions (items 9, 14, 15, 16, 17). We will not reopen §§3.1/3.3 (usage-based fees), §10.2, §10.5 or §6.3, each of which is at or better than our preferred position.
7. **Escalate to the deal principal** if HDI refuses any of the walk-away items in section 3, in particular the vendor indemnity and the data-return obligation.

---

*Note on verification: the findings above are as supplied by the review; automated verification was not run on any item. Section references and conclusions are drawn solely from the supplied findings.*"}

## 3. Walk-away items

The following findings sit in, approach, or risk the playbook's walk-away territory and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than negotiable preferences:

1. **No vendor indemnity at all (item 1, INDEMN — critical).** The complete absence of any IP indemnity is expressly walk-away under the rule. HDI must accept the §9A package.
2. **No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data (item 18, INSURANCE).** Walk-away under the rule; HDI hosts the Site and holds user information. The E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback is available as a landing zone, but some cyber cover is non-negotiable.
3. **No data return on exit (item 11, TRANSITION).** The Agreement falls below the fallback and risks the walk-away outcome of no data return, with §10.7 survival omitting §§4, 5 and 8. We must have the §4.3 return-and-deletion obligation.
4. **Uncapped Termination Payment (items 5 and 6, LD / T4C).** The §4.2(a) payment approaches walk-away territory: it is uncapped, can exceed remaining contract value, and applies even when we terminate for HDI's breach. At minimum it must be disapplied on HDI breach.
5. **Unlimited inspection frequency (item 13, AUDIT).** §3.4 has no frequency cap at all, approaching the walk-away position on unlimited audits. A once-per-twelve-month cap is a minimal, low-cost fix.
6. **Unlimited liability with no cap and nothing to carve out (item 3, LOL-CAP).** Exposure to unlimited direct and consequential damages is not acceptable, and the cap and the indemnity in item 1 should be negotiated together.
7. **No ownership of our own customer data or the Site deliverables (item 2, IP).** Read with item 11, we currently have neither title to nor a contractual right to recover the data HDI holds.
